propositions: Transport parameters in core reconciler modules are unannotated or annotated through unresolvable import paths (rebar_reconciler.*), causing mypy to widen them to Any and lose attribute checking despite appear being typed

Relative imports inside reconciler modules (from ._backend import) make the port type resolvable to mypy, enabling [attr-defined] errors for undeclared members, while unresolvable absolute imports silently degrade to Any

Four opt-in capability members (add_comment, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map) are carried as metaclass attributes and are unreachable by mypy's protocol attribute collection, so sites using them without narrowing to a capability Protocol are invisible to the AST audit but caught by mypy

The custom metaclass _TransportPortMeta is load-bearing for runtime conformance checking (uncached isinstance) but does not prevent mypy attribute checking when the port type is resolvably imported, contrary to earlier investigation

Annotating transport parameters as the port type AND importing it through a resolvable path (relative import or TYPE_CHECKING guard) enables mypy to enforce port completeness; annotating alone or via the unresolvable shim path produces annotations that silently enforce nothing
